newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA Peugeot Citroen H1 profit cut in half.
newsitem.headline: PSA Peugeot Citroen H1 profit cut in half.

text.p: French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen reported on Monday that its first-half profit shrank by more than half in the first six months of 1996 as weak growth in car sales and a fierce price war eroded its margins.

The company reported net attributable profit fell to 602 million francs ($117.5 million) in the first half of 1996 from 1.22 billion francs, and its operating margin shrank to 1.34 billion francs from 2.78 billion.
Its stock fell 1.54 percent to 574 francs in early trading on the bourse, although the profit fall came as no surprise.
The Peugeot group's French rival, Renault SA, earlier this month reported a huge drop in first-half profit to 158 million francs from 1.76 billion.

PSA Peugeot Citroen said in a statement that its first-half performance was weakened by a price war in its domestic market and the franc's strength relative to other currencies despite recent gains in the Italian lira.
"In this context, PSA Peugeot Citroen sought the best balance between unit margins and volumes," it said.

Although its unit sales rose just one percent, the group's turnover increased three percent to 89.04 billion francs as it improved its product mix and sold more expensive models in its line-up, including the new Peugeot 406 saloon.
The company said European currency shifts, namely slight gains in currencies that were previously devalued, and lower French interest rates would help second-half results.

The French car industry faces an uncertain outlook in the second half. Car sales are surging ahead of the expiry on September 30 of a year-long new-cars-for-old incentive scheme, but sales are expected to plunge in the fourth quarter.

A fierce price war waged by foreign manufacturers in the French market shows no sign of letting up and is likely to cut into the French companies' profit margins and increase pressure on them to reduce their costs. ($ = 5.125 French Francs)
